title: hello
description: Opens a connection: the protocol versions the client speaks, who it is, and optionally the client id it resumes. Every other method before hello is bad_request, reason hello_required. hello is the one tolerant method: a host ignores params fields it does not know, at every depth. Its result is a host's or a hub's, told apart by endpoint.kind (plan 027 X5): clientId, token, resumed and retryHorizon are a host's alone.

protocols.description: Every protocol version the client speaks; the host answers with the highest it shares.

auth.description: Reserved for S6: absent or null.

via.description: Reserved for a hub or relay that originates the host connection itself (S4/S7): absent or null.

clientCapabilities.description: The client's own capability set: empty in protocol 1.

resume.description: The client id to take back and the token hello handed it. A matching token in the same engine incarnation resumes; a retired client or another incarnation gets a fresh id (resumed: false); a wrong token is bad_request, reason bad_token.

result.description: A host's result or a hub's, told apart by endpoint.kind (plan 027 X5).

resultFields.description: The members every hello result carries, host's and hub's alike.

protocol.description: The highest version both sides speak.

hostResult.description: A host's result (endpoint.kind host): the connection's client id and resume token, whether a resume took, and the command-id table's bound, all four always present (resumed: false included). They are a host's alone: client ids, tokens and receipts are always the host's.

clientId.description: The connection's client id, bound to it, never sent per call.

token.description: Resumes clientId on a later connection to this host, within this engine incarnation.

resumed.description: The resume took: only then does a client resend its in-flight commands under their own ids.

hubResult.description: A hub's result (endpoint.kind hub, S4's hub mode): no client id, token, resumed or retry horizon — a hub mints no client ids and keeps no receipts — and carrying any of them is invalid. A client spliced to a host (session.connect) says hello to the host itself.

endpointFields.description: Who answered: its id (a host's is sessions.list's epoch), craze's version and its pid.

codecs.description: The event and snapshot codecs' own versions. A client that does not know one must not fold that stream.

limits.description: The line limits, in bytes: the longest line the host reads (4 MiB) and the longest it writes, which a client must accept (16 MiB).

errorResult.description: data.result beside a protocol_version refusal: the versions the host speaks.
